findings.reason: as written the node deletes a guard on a seam the plan did not analyse, regressing a resume/lane-change launch to an attempt number below the one the pointer records, for a race that the disk-keyed reservation already prevents.
findings.text: §16 justifies removing the launch-attempt floor ("It launches the reservation's attempt instead, and takes no floor from its own record") by saying a door-local floor would let a resume and a dispatch racing on a marker-only run compute *different keys*; but the key is `launch_reservation_key`, computed from disk only, so a floor cannot change it and cannot produce that race. What the floor at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:3088` actually guards is the compatibility seam at `dispatch_launch.py:1642`, which fires for `resume-*` and `lane-change-*` stream paths and passes **no** reservation into `supervised_launch`; on that path `reserved_here` is true and the floor is the only thing between a run whose pointer names attempt N with no receipt on disk (key = 1) and a launch at attempt 1 — the case the code's own comment at :3082-3085 names ("its record may name an attempt that left no receipt at all"). The primary resume door (`resumption.py:1724`) reserves before calling `supervised_launch` and never takes the floor at all, so the door the plan describes is not the door the removed line serves.

findings.reason: the paragraph names `_record_reservation_supervisor` explicitly, so the worker can still find the site; the stale line only costs a lookup.
findings.text: §16 cites the supervisor-record write as "`dispatch_launch.py` near line 2440"; at this base line 2440 is `_create_reservation`, and `record_reservation_supervisor`'s `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` write is at `dispatch_launch.py:2514`, so the pointer names a different function than the one whose suppression the section repairs.
